read_PR_discussions.title: Lock a used safety needle's hinged sheath one-handed by pressing it on the table, then put the syringe in a sharps tray by AMMistry18 · Pull Request #2049 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: The robot makes a used safety needle safe the way the maker's instructions allow: one-handed, by pressing the hinged safety sheath against a firm surface until it clicks shut over the needle, then dropping the syringe into a sharps tray. Medical assistants, registered nurses and LPNs give injections as regular work ("Administer medications to patients...", "performing such tasks as giving injections"), and shielding the needle straight after every injection is the step that prevents needlestick injuries. A real-size 3 mL safety syringe with a 25 G x 1 in needle lies beside a practice injection pad. The robot picks it up by the 10.5 mm barrel, rocks the open sheath down onto the table so it swings around the needle on its hinge, and presses until the sprung catch clicks (about 3 N), then puts the syringe in the tray. The other gripper must never come within 100 mm of the bare needle, the sheath must be locked against the table (not the pad, the tray or the other gripper), and the needle must not touch the pad or tray: any of these zeroes the trial. task.json : instruction, setup, scoring, run limit, fidelity and scores README.md : run and score commands, syringe, sheath, catch, pad and tray dimensions, scoring, the scripted demo, the real-trial plan (blunt-ground real unit) and how to check the click force on a real unit close_safety_needle_shield_one_handed.py : scene (syringe with a hinged U-channel sheath around a separate needle and a sprung catch, pad, tray), scorer and scripted demo yam_parts.py , yam_joints.py : kit modules, copied unchanged test_close_safety_needle_shield_one_handed.py : offline checks of the scorer on goal, partial-credit and cheat layouts, and of the demo's reach 🤖 Generated with Claude Code
